# The fleet, at human scale

**51,134,071,679 tokens** across 17,116 sessions on 5 computer(s), every CLI.

_Counts are exact — they are what each provider's API reported. Everything phrased as a comparison is approximate: a token is roughly 0.75 English words, and that ratio moves with language and with how much of the text is code._

### Three totals, and why they differ

They are not competing answers; they answer different questions, and adding them together would be meaningless.

| number | what it counts | where |
|---:|---|---|
| **51,134,071,679** | every CLI, per session, still on disk | this file |
| **44,068,164,067** | Claude Code only, per account | BY-ACCOUNT.md |
| **higher still** | + the frozen lifetime counter, for work whose transcripts were deleted | the floor table in BY-COMPUTER.md |

This file counts what survives on disk. Claude Code deletes transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays`, so the real usage is larger than anything here — the floor table is the closest defensible figure, and it is still a floor.

## Most of it is the same text, read again

This is the correction that matters most, and the first version of this file got it wrong. A conversation resends its entire history on every turn, and those resends are billed as `cache_read` tokens. They are real tokens and real spend — but they are not new writing, and comparing them to books implies they are.

| | tokens | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| re-read from cache | 41,646,612,045 |  94.7% |
| written to cache | 1,750,985,239 |   4.0% |
| sent fresh | 404,739,425 |   0.9% |
| **generated by the model** | 183,582,067 |   0.4% |

**2,339,306,731 tokens were new content** — everything else is the conversation being re-sent. On the machine this was written on, one chat of 2,613 turns cost 1,301,790,690 tokens, of which 3,089,179 (0.24%) was generated text.

## If you tried to read it

Counting only the **new** content — 1.75 billion words. The billed total would give a figure about 19× larger, and would be counting the same sentences over and over.

| that is | roughly |
|---|---:|
| War and Peace | **2,987×** |
| the King James Bible | **2,240×** |
| the Harry Potter series | **1,618×** |
| the complete works of Shakespeare | **1,983×** |
| English Wikipedia | **37.3% of it** |
| read aloud at 130 words/min, without stopping | **25.7 years** |
| typed at 40 words/min, without stopping | **83.5 years** |

_Busiest day counts each session on the date it STARTED; a session running past midnight lands entirely on the earlier date._

Total measured session time: **1,109 hours** (0.13 years of wall clock).

_Duration is a judgement call, not a measurement — it is the span between a session's first and last message, and a session left open overnight counts the night. Treat it as an upper bound._
